rounds.text: Aprameya Engineering Ltd trades at a modest market capitalisation of ₹ 194 Cr [E3], backed by a tangible price-to-book ratio of just 2.80x on a book value of ₹ 36.4 against a share price of ₹ 102 [E2]. Operational efficiency outshines the wider market context, as demonstrated by a return on assets of 6.61% that successfully clears the sector benchmark of 6.35% [E8]. Furthermore, the company operates within a robust macro environment supported by a sector median profit growth of 19.0% [E50]. Conceded: [E4], [E5], [E6], [E7], [E11], [E15], [E32], [E33], [E34], [E36], [E45].

Aprameya Engineering Ltd carries a severe valuation disconnect and negative momentum, sitting a mere 2% up its 52-week range from a high of 360 down to a low of 98 [E5]. This depressed price action is fully justified by fundamental deterioration, highlighted by a catastrophic compounded profit growth of -68% over the trailing twelve months [E15]. Multiple valuation metrics demonstrate profound overpricing relative to peers, with the EV/EBITDA surging to 35.29x against a sector benchmark of just 17.95x [E11], alongside a trailing P/E of 75.99x dwarfing the 33.16x sector benchmark [E6]. Conceded: the company maintains a return on assets of 6.61% that slightly edges out the sector benchmark of 6.35% [E8], and its price-to-book stands at a more moderate 2.80x based on filed statements [E2].

Conceded: trailing profit growth stands at -68% [E15], and a discounted cash flow calculates an intrinsic value of ₹ 62 per share [E32]. However, the market price has already violently corrected to ₹ 102, sitting just 2% above its 52-week low of 98, which effectively flushes out prior froth and prices in the historical earnings contraction [E5]. Furthermore, filed statements show a much more reasonable trailing P/E of 38.1x and a modest price-to-book of 2.80x based on a book value of ₹ 36.4, making the provider's headline valuation multiples look heavily overstated [E1, E2]. Crucially, Aprameya generates an operational return on assets of 6.61%, outperforming the sector benchmark of 6.35% [E8]. This proves the underlying asset base remains efficient and profitable, providing a solid operational foundation to capitalize on broader sector tailwinds where median profit growth runs at 19.0% [E50].

Conceded: the operational return on assets reaches 6.61%, outperforming the sector benchmark of 6.35% [E8]. However, the bull claims the violent correction to ₹ 102—sitting at 2% of its 52-week range—flushes out prior froth [E5], yet a reverse DCF demonstrates that today's price still implies an aggressive 16.9% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of just 10.0% [E34]. While the bull points to filed statements showing a trailing P/E of 38.1x and a P/B of 2.80x to dismiss data provider metrics [E1, E2], the data provider highlights an even more alarming P/E of 75.99x versus a sector benchmark of 33.16x alongside a P/B of 5.59x [E6, E7], proving valuation remains severely inflated across multiple lenses. Furthermore, pointing to sector tailwinds of 19.0% median profit growth [E50] ignores the company's catastrophic trailing profit contraction of -68% [E15]. Finally, the claim that prices reflect the downturn is undone by the reality that price growth currently exceeds profit growth by 3%, confirming expectations are still running dangerously ahead of delivery [E36].
